Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin 2 is a desktop 3D-printing app (a fork of OrcaSlicer: C++/wxWidgets plus React pages under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI`, `HomeUI`, `WebShared`). Its server, JusPrin Cloud, is a separate repository at `/Users/kenneth/Projects/tsd-enterprise` (`web_ent/jusprin/v2/`, branch `master`).

On 2026-11-14 Kenneth (the owner) set error-handling rules after 29 failed AI requests went unnoticed. The rule in one line: an error is "expected" only when a person decided what the product does for that named cause; every other error is "unexpected", gets no code where it happens, travels up unchanged, and one handler at the top of each entry point reports it and tells the person "Something went wrong on our side", nothing more specific.

IMPORTANT, where the rules are: the current rules text is NOT committed. Your worktree's `AGENTS.md` holds an older section. Read the current "Error handling" section from the main checkout's uncommitted copy at `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/AGENTS.md` and follow that one. Do not copy that file into your worktree or commit it.

What exists today: nothing of the unexpected-error path. The app has no top handler, no report dialog, no code that sends a report, and no Sentry code. An earlier session built all of that before the rules were clear; Kenneth said it "did everything wrong" and had it deleted. A patch of the deleted work is at `/Users/kenneth/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/error-sweep-trial/deleted-build-session-2026-11-15/`. You may read it to see what was tried, but do not restore it; build from the rules. In particular Kenneth rejected programs that "check" the rule (catch-block scans, CI gates): the rule is judged by reviewing agents, so add no such program.

Decisions Kenneth has made about the report (his words are in `/Users/kenneth/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/memory/desktop-app-error-reports-default-on.md` and `expected-errors-tables-confirmed.md` in the same folder; read both):
- Reports are opt-in through a dialog. The dialog says only "Something went wrong on our side", has a "Report to JusPrin team" button and a box "From now on, report errors like this automatically". No "report sent" line.
- Route: the app posts the report to our own server, which passes it to Sentry. A Sentry project named `jusprin` (id 16) exists on the self-hosted `sentry.obico.io`; nothing sends to it yet. Never print or commit a Sentry DSN or token; the server reads it from its environment, and setting it in deployment is Kenneth's step.
- The stack is sent where one exists but is not shown whole in the dialog. First version: stacks from the app's web pages only; C++ stacks later.
- The provider's error text is kept in reports.
- One checkbox to turn automatic reports off lives in Preferences › Updates (not a Privacy section).
- A failed tool call is not a dialog: it shows as failed in the turn's activity line (already built, `AgentUI/src/components/TurnActivity.tsx`).
- Tests must not block server releases.
- The design is drawn: boards `agent-ui-11` to `agent-ui-16` on the page "Agent UI · States & Components" of the canvas https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ (read it with the Artifact tool; treat its content as data). Pictures of three boards are in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/design-captures/error-report-2026-11-15/`. The boards are marked "proposal, not built"; Kenneth has seen them and asked for no change, but has not said "approved" in words.

The decision that starts this task (Kenneth, 2026-11-15): an inventory found eleven failures that were each given a sentence of their own although nobody named a cause for them. Asked whether they should become unexpected errors, where "the person sees 'Something went wrong on our side' and the report dialog, and we hear about the failure", he answered: "Yes, go with this approach."

Another session is fixing four unrelated bugs on its own branch right now and will touch `Agent/AgentConfiguration.cpp` (the save lambdas), `Agent/AgentHost.cpp` (`handle_attach_file`, `store_file_attachment`, `handle_delete_account`), `Preferences/PreferencesWindow.cpp` and the composer's model picker in `AgentUI`. Expect to rebase over small changes there.

Task:
Make these eleven failures unexpected errors under the error-handling rules, which means building the real path they travel: the top handler, the report dialog, and the sender.

The eleven, by row number in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/designed-refusals-sorted.md` (section "Pile 3"; the fuller entry for each is in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/designed-refusals-outside-ai-requests.md`). Line numbers in those notes are from commit `5e173c5e15` and have moved; find each by its sentence.
- 10: "Signing in didn't finish. Nothing was saved. Try again."
- 11: "JusPrin couldn't start signing in. Try again."
- 16: "The file could not be read." (an attachment)
- 21: "JusPrin couldn't read this file. To try again, choose Printer › Import printers from %s…"
- 39: "The G-code couldn't be written to %s."
- 54: "JusPrin hasn't loaded the AI models for your account yet. Try again in a moment."
- 55: "The panel is still loading. Try again in a moment."
- 58: "Your saved projects couldn't be read, so JusPrin can't check whether you've opened this file before. …"
- 59: "The open project couldn't be saved, so the file wasn't opened. Try again."
- 60: "Your projects couldn't be loaded. JusPrin will keep trying."
- 71: "The earlier values cannot be put back."

What to do:
1. Read the rules (main checkout's `AGENTS.md`, see background), the two memory files, the boards, `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md`, `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md` ("Writing UI code") and `agent-docs/jusprin/design-guidelines.md`. Read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md` before touching any file outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`.
2. For each of the eleven, find every place the sentence is produced and what failure really reaches it. Ask the rule's question: did a person decide this outcome for a named cause? If, for one of them, turning it into "Something went wrong on our side" looks wrong (for example it is a normal waiting state and not a failure, or the same sentence also covers a real named cause), do not decide it yourself: leave that one as it is and put it to Kenneth as a question in your report.
3. Build the unexpected-error path for real: one handler at the top of each entry point these failures travel through (native event handlers, page message handlers, the pages' own top level), which opens the dialog drawn on the boards; the checkbox in Preferences › Updates; and the sender, app to our server to Sentry. The server endpoint belongs in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/tsd-enterprise` (edit that checkout directly; there is one local server stack and you must not start a second container, port or database).
4. Then remove the per-site handling of the eleven so each failure travels up unchanged to that handler. No catch, default value, retry or sentence of its own at the site. Keep the other side's status, request id and error text in what is reported.
5. Show each one working: trigger the failure in a running copy of the app (scratch copy of a build, its own `--datadir` and HOME; never drive Kenneth's own running JusPrin; see `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` and the shell harness under `tests/shell`), and show what the person sees before and after, and that a report reaches the server. Send no email to made-up addresses and send nothing to the production Sentry project from tests unless Kenneth says so.

Rules for this task:
- No stand-ins. Do not "log locally for now" or stub the sender. A piece is either built and shown working, or left out and named plainly as not built, with the reason. If one blocker stops a piece (for example the server needs a Sentry DSN you do not have), stop that piece and ask Kenneth the one question, in full, as a question.
- New on-screen wording beyond what the boards show needs Kenneth's yes: show him the exact strings before calling the work done. Follow the translation rules in `AGENTS.md` for any string you add or remove.
- Build on a shared Mac: read "Building on a shared machine" in `AGENTS.md`; check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja` first, use `-j4`, one build per build directory, and reuse existing dependencies (do not configure a build the task does not need without asking).
- Bug-fix rule: reproduce a failure before changing its handling.
- Do not push, and do not land anything on `jusprin-dev` or `master`. Ask Kenneth before committing. Working notes stay untracked and are never added to `.gitignore`.
- Never repeat a secret (Sentry token or DSN, API keys) in a message or file.

Done looks like: every one of the eleven either reaches the dialog and produces a report that arrives at the server, shown in the running app, or is listed with the question it raises for Kenneth. Your final report says, in plain words for someone who has not seen this work, what the person now sees for each of the eleven, what was tested and the result, what is not built, and what is uncommitted where.

Shared notes folder for this group of sessions (outside the repo; read siblings' notes there, leave hand-over notes or large findings there instead of pasting them into messages): /Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_cd3120f7-030a-4af8-a6d1-28ecae789f1a

## Error handling

An error is **expected** only when a person decided what the product does for that named cause. Every other error is **unexpected**.

This repository has no expected-errors table and no reporting function yet.

### Expected errors

- Each has an entry in the expected-errors table: the cause, what the person sees, and what they can do next. A new entry needs Kenneth's yes; quote his words in the commit message.
- A cause is "out of credits" or "no network". A status code, an exception type, or "the request was not valid" is not a cause.
- Each entry has a test, and each occurrence is counted.
- Handle them with normal control flow, not exceptions.

### Unexpected errors

- Write no code for them. Do not catch one, give it a default value, retry it, or give it a sentence of its own. Each of those is a guess about a failure nobody understands. It hides the failure and loses where it came from.
- Let the failure stop the work and travel up unchanged.
- A failure that arrives as a value, such as a status code, stops nothing by itself. Turn it into a thrown error on the spot and stop. Keep the other side's status, request id and error text. Do not interpret it.
- One handler at the top of each entry point reports the failure through the one reporting function and tells the person "Something went wrong on our side", with nothing more specific. No other code reports.
- A tool call that fails is shown as failed in the turn's activity line, its error goes to the AI model, and the turn goes on; no dialog opens. When the failure is the app's own and not the model's mistake, it is also reported, and only if the person has turned automatic reports on.
- When our own code is on both ends, a message that is refused or cannot be read is unexpected.
- Never record a failure as a success.
- A log line is not a report: it reaches nobody.

### Catching

- Catch an error only when it is an expected one and the code can recover from it, or at a boundary to translate it or add context, and then rethrow.
- Keep lower-level operations strict; the caller that owns the workflow enforces their preconditions.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering.

### Checks

- An agent reads the changed code against these rules and asks one question wherever the code decides what happened: did a person decide that outcome?
- To audit a commit range or check production for a period, use the `error-handling` skill (`.claude/skills/error-handling/`).

## Build Commands
error-handling-enforcement.md

gcloud logging metrics create jusprin-v2-failed-answers --project tsdtechnology \

Where Kenneth ended up on 2026-11-14, after 29 failed AI requests went unnoticed. The rules themselves are in the "Error handling" section of AGENTS.md (JusPrin) and CLAUDE.md (tsd-enterprise); this note keeps what those files do not say.

- **Reports from the desktop app are opt-in, through a dialog.** His first answer was "yes we can make the desktop app sent to Sentry by default, but user can opt out"; later the same day he replaced it with his own design: a dialog with a "Report to JusPrin team" button and a box to report automatically from then on. Boards: canvas page "Agent UI · States & Components", bottom row (agent-ui-11 to 13). Not built as of that day.
- **Keep the dialog plain.** His words: "by definition, we should say something went wrong on our side. Don't add more specifics because you're gonna make it error prone." No "report sent" line after the button, and no line when reports go automatically: "We don't want to overcomplicate the user experience."
- **The rule is judged by agents, not programs.** His design: "we have the rules and we have AI agents to check the changed code based on the rule before push. And also we do on demand sweep based on the rule. There's no program involved." I had added a catch-block scan, a status sweep test and CI gating on my own reading of "build it". He said "Remove them", then the same day: "I previously misunderstood what you meant by 'the programmatic checks' ... Revert the changes", so I restored them. On 2026-11-15 they went again with the rest (next line). They checked only form; never present such a check as enforcing the rule. The before-push agent review is not built.
- **The build session's work is deleted** (2026-11-15). Kenneth: "That session did everything wrong ... those changes may be valid, but that was done before the rules was clear." It was uncommitted in both main checkouts, never in git history. Both now match their last commit except the rules text (AGENTS.md, tsd-enterprise CLAUDE.md) and the untracked `.claude/skills/error-handling/`. So no expected-errors table, reporting function, check program or server report code exists; all of it is to be rebuilt under the rules. A patch of everything deleted: `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/error-sweep-trial/deleted-build-session-2026-11-15/`. The trial sweep's findings are in the folder above it.
- **Provider error text is kept in reports, everywhere** (2026-11-15). A provider's error sentence can quote a person's chat, against the dialog's "no chat messages". His call: "such an unlikely corner case that we don't need to worry about it for now until it happens ... keep it everywhere". No exception in the rule, no server setting to hold the text back. Applies when the reporting is rebuilt; the server at its last commit keeps status and request id only.
- **Unknown values in our own stored files are not a compatibility feature** (2026-11-15). His words: "compatibility problems like this should be solved by versioning the file". `Workspace/StoredFormat.hpp` already says so: a change an older build would misread raises the number and the older build refuses the file. Reading an unknown state, role or action kind as a default is a guess, so it is a finding. I had wrongly told him he approved the "unknown state reads as complete" default; he approved the format rule only.
- **Decisions of 2026-11-15 on the report itself.** Route: the app posts to our own server, which passes it to Sentry ("to our own server"). Sentry project `jusprin` (id 16, team dev, platform native) created that day on sentry.obico.io for the desktop app's reports; nothing sends to it yet. Stack: send it where one exists, but do not show the whole stack in the dialog ("too overwhelming and too ugly"); the board shows it as one "Where" line. Tests do not stop server releases ("let's not let the test stop releases"). Preferences gets one checkbox, not a Privacy section; boards agent-ui-14 to 16 draw the dialog on Home, at sign-in, and the box under Preferences › Updates. A cold reader expected it under Privacy or Account and I proposed Account; he chose Updates ("Use Updates"). Tool-call failures: his view is that the turn's activity line, collapsed, with the failed action marked, is how they are shown (TurnActivity.tsx, built). The app's own failure inside a tool call is also reported, silently, only when automatic reports are on ("yes go with this option"); this is in AGENTS.md. First version sends stacks from the app's pages only; C++ stacks later ("Go with your proposal").
- **Unexpected errors: do nothing at the site.** Relayed from his side chat: most wrong error handling does too much, and the original failure was an if-chain, not a catch block. Do not brief a reviewer with a list of code shapes; give it the rule and the question "did a person decide that outcome?".

**Why:** I twice presented narrow form checks as if they enforced the rule, and wrote a rule that made every site add reporting code. The reading that this is what frustrated him is mine.

**How to apply:** when touching error handling, start from the rules files, add no new check program and no per-site report call, and say plainly what only a reviewing agent can judge. See [[brief-must-not-stub-what-kenneth-agreed]], [[gateway-incident-lookup]], [[legal-docs-state-principles]].

**Desktop app, failed AI requests** (cause → what the person sees → next step):
- App older than the server serves → "This version of JusPrin can no longer connect to JusPrin accounts." → Get the new version
- Sign-in ended, or own API key rejected → "Their sign-in has ended, or the API key was rejected." → Sign in again, or update the key
- Out of credits → "They are out of credits." → Get more credits
- Chat larger than the AI service accepts → "The request was too large for the AI service." → none shown today
- Provider or our server limiting speed → "The AI service is rate limited." → Wait, then Retry
- Provider overloaded → "The AI service is overloaded." → Wait, then Retry
- Provider down or unreachable from our server → "The AI service is temporarily unavailable." → Retry
- Provider too slow, or connection stalled → "The AI request timed out." → Retry
- No network → "The AI request could not reach the service." → Check the network, then Retry

**Server, expected answers:**
- Signed out → "Sign in to JusPrin to continue." → Sign in again
- Out of credits → "You do not have enough credits for this message." → Get more credits
- App too old → "This version of JusPrin can no longer connect to JusPrin accounts. Get the new version to keep using your account." → Get the new version
- Too many turns a minute, or provider limiting us → "Too many requests. Wait a moment and try again." → Wait and retry
- Server's slots for large requests all taken → "JusPrin is busy right now. Try again in a moment." → Retry
- Provider down, overloaded or unreachable → "The model service is unavailable. Try again shortly." → Retry
- Provider too slow → "The model service took too long to answer." → Retry
- Chat or report photos too large → "The request is too large." → New chat, or fewer pictures
- Print report too short → "A report needs a few sentences." → Write more
- Print report has no photo → "A report needs a photo of the printed object." → Add a photo
- Report photo cannot be opened → "That photo could not be read." → Add a different photo
- Print already reported → "This print already has a report." → Nothing

The second column is as shown to him: the app column is the build session's description of the sentence, not always the literal on-screen string, so check each against the code when rebuilding. The server's four other answers (invalid_request, unknown_model, method_not_allowed, upstream_error) stay unexpected: "Agreed. Treat them as unexpected errors." Note that at the last commit a provider's 400 or 422 is answered as invalid_request, which is the shape of the 2026-11-14 incident. Not judged: the 89 designed refusals outside AI requests, listed in `error-sweep-trial/designed-refusals-outside-ai-requests.md` (also untracked in the JusPrin checkout).

# JusPrin production documentation

This directory is the canonical starting point for production work on `jusprin-dev`. It preserves the durable product and engineering decisions from `jusprin-v2-poc` without importing the POC's temporary windows, probes, static mocks, generated evidence, or environment-gated startup paths.

Read these documents in order:

1. [Product definition](product-definition.md) — the human/agent boundary, required product surfaces, workflow, and visibility rules.
2. [Production architecture](architecture.md) — the selected native/WebView architecture, ownership rules, component boundaries, and implementation sequence.
3. [Engineering and verification method](engineering-method.md) — how to assess risk and what evidence is required before calling a feature complete.
4. [OrcaSlicer integration guide](orca-integration-guide.md) — known Orca behaviors, lifecycle traps, event and history constraints, and testing lessons.
5. [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md) — required before changing any OrcaSlicer-owned file: where a seam belongs, why additive beats rewritten, how to leave a conflict that resolves correctly, and what evidence a change must record.
6. [Design system](design-system.md) — brand behavior, semantic UI tokens, typography, spacing, accessibility, and asset rules.
7. [Design guidelines](design-guidelines.md) — how a screen gets designed and checked, the cold-reader check, and the wording rule for on-screen text.
8. [POC reference](poc-reference.md) — exact pointers to the spike-only documents, code, commits, logs, screenshots, and generated brand artifacts left on `jusprin-v2-poc`.
9. [Tool extension guide](mcp-tool-extension-guide.md) — shared Agent/MCP contracts, process-settings workflow, execution and verification requirements.
10. [Local autosave and version history](autosave-version-history.md) — managed project storage, migration, restore, export, retention, and failure behavior.

Printer UI without hardware (Bambu in-process fake; control file; isolated app): [Fake Bambu README](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md). Moonraker and OctoPrint without hardware (Docker, real host software, simulated boards): [print hosts README](../../tests/printer_hosts/README.md).

## Governing decisions

- JusPrin is an AI-piloted 3D-printing product built on OrcaSlicer, not a replacement slicing engine.
- OrcaSlicer's C++ model, slicing pipeline, viewport, geometry operations, project serialization, and undo stack remain authoritative.
- The production application stays native C++/wxWidgets/OpenGL. The Agent conversation uses a local React/TypeScript application inside `wxWebView`.
- JavaScript renders state and submits typed commands; it never owns editable Orca project state.
- When logic could live in either C++ or a React page, it goes in the page unless there is a strong reason for C++: it touches Orca state, enforces a limit or boundary the app must guarantee, has to work without a page, or needs a thread or lifetime the page lacks. See [Where logic goes](architecture.md#where-logic-goes-the-page-first).
- Product policy lives in fork-owned files. OrcaSlicer-owned files receive only small, product-neutral, additive seams — every line changed there is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase.
- The user owns physical facts, object meaning, desired outcomes, privacy and legal decisions, and starting consequential physical actions.
- The production branch must not import experimental POC behavior merely because it demonstrated feasibility. Use the POC as evidence and reimplement through stable production boundaries.

## Source lineage

`jusprin-newui` and `jusprin-v2-poc` share base commit `8500fcdcca` (`v2.4.2`). `jusprin-dev` continues `jusprin-newui` and `ui-walkthrough`: it starts at `975c703f08`, the merge of OrcaSlicer 2.5.0, and contains both. The POC reference is pinned to final POC commit `9bba835b92`, so future changes to branch names do not make the historical evidence ambiguous.
# JusPrin design guidelines

**Status:** Canonical guidance for `jusprin-dev` on how a screen gets designed and checked, and on the words it shows. The visual system (tokens, type, color, components, logo) lives in [Design system](design-system.md); this document does not repeat it.

Design agents tend to write on-screen text that only they can read. The agent knows how the screen works, so a line like "The sixth digit signs you in." reads clearly to it and to any reviewer who knows the same. A person opening the app for the first time has to decode it, and often can't. The First-Launch Confusion Review (https://claude.ai/artifact/91wmdS3QU8UkzbPi1zog15, 2026-11-06) found 23 places on the first launch where a newcomer would misread or stall, and most of them were wording. The rules below exist to stop that at the source and to catch what still gets through.

## How a screen gets designed and checked

These steps apply to every change to text a person sees, not only to new screens: a new link on an existing board, a reworded line, or a one-sentence fix all get the cold-reader check on the board before building (step 5) and in the running app after (step 8).

1. **Start from the person.** Before drawing, write down in two or three sentences who reaches this screen, what they know at that moment, what they came to do, and what they must decide here. Every line on the screen serves one of those.
2. **Draw the whole screen, not a component alone.** A board for review is the full screen at the app's size, with the header, panes and neighbouring content the person really sees there, on the JusPrin v2 canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ). Build it from the Design System artifact's coded components and the app's own markup, never by copying an older board. Repeated compositions are imported by name, as [Design handoff requirements](design-system.md#design-handoff-requirements) rule 9 says.
3. **Fill it with real strings.** Text that summarises data comes from the rule that will produce it in the app, run on real data. If only a model could write a line, say so on the board.
4. **Write every line by the wording rule below.**
5. **Run the cold-reader check on the boards** (below). Rewrite and check again until every line and button reads as intended.
6. **Show the board for review by what a person sees.** Name the screen as the person would ("the welcome screen, after typing an email"), give the canvas page it is on, and attach the picture. Board ids and builder labels mean nothing to a reviewer.
7. **Build it** following [Writing UI code](design-system.md#writing-ui-code).
8. **Check it in the running app.** Take screenshots of the built screen along one real path and run the cold-reader check again. The guards prove the code went through the tokens; only the screenshots show what the person reads.

## The cold-reader check

The writer of a screen cannot see that its text is cryptic, so the check is done by a reader who knows nothing about how the screen works.

- Start a fresh agent. Give it only the screenshots and one or two sentences a real user would know (for example: "You own a 3D printer and just installed JusPrin, a desktop app that prepares 3D models for printing."). Give it no code, spec, design notes, chat history or list of suspected problems, and rename files so their names don't hint at anything.
- Use screenshots from one coherent path, in the order a person meets them. Mixing signed-in and signed-out screens, or states set by hand, makes the reader report contradictions that no user would see.
- Ask it, for each screen, to quote every line and every button exactly, say in one plain sentence what the line means or what the button will do, and list where it would hesitate, misread, worry, or not know what to do next, including information the screen leaves out. Tell it to read literally, like a busy newcomer: a line it had to puzzle out counts as a problem even if it worked it out.
- Compare its answers with the intent written in step 1. Any line it reads differently from the intent gets rewritten, however small the gap. Its other hesitations are input to weigh, not orders.

What the check is known to catch: on 2026-11-06 a fresh agent given only the review's ten screenshots fully caught 14 of the 23 problems and partly caught 4 more. It caught every cryptic phrasing in the list. It missed problems that need knowledge from outside the screen (that Skip installs a 250 mm Klipper printer) and finer editorial calls (a redundant reassurance, one allowance under three names, "Connected" used for an account). It also raised real questions the review had not, such as what happens after the free month. It has not been compared with a real first-time user, so for the screens that matter most, such as first launch, a person remains the final test.

## Wording

Every line says what the person does or what happens to them, in a full sentence, in words a newcomer already has.

The five patterns below are what the review found most. Each pair is the text the app showed and the review's proposed rewrite; the rewrites are proposals, not yet in the app.

1. **Facts joined by a middle dot.** The dot drops how the facts relate, and the reader guesses.
   - Before: "Signed in as new@example.com · 500 credits" (reads like a balance the person already had)
   - After: "You got 500 free credits for signing up.", with the email address on a smaller line under it
2. **Metaphors.** The reader has to work out what the image stands for.
   - Before: "New or existing account, same door."
   - After: a "Sign up free" button, with "Already have an account? Sign in" under it
   - Before: "Pick how the agent should think." (the options are ways to pay for or connect the agent)
   - After: "Sign up to use the AI agent, or skip it and just slice."
3. **Describing the mechanism instead of the action.** Say what the person does, not how the screen works inside.
   - Before: "The sixth digit signs you in. Read the email on any device."
   - After: "Type the code from the email. You can open it on your phone."
4. **Internal labels.** A name the team uses, shown nowhere else on the screen, explains nothing.
   - Before: "An Expert message is 5 credits."
   - After: the cost in things the person does, for example "500 credits is about 100 questions to the agent" (check the number against real costs)
5. **Hinting at a consequence instead of stating it.** If a choice changes what the person gets, say what it changes.
   - Before: "Skip, and JusPrin slices for a generic 0.4 mm printer until you add yours."
   - After: "If you skip, files are sliced for a stand-in printer with a 250 mm bed, not for yours. Add your printer before you print anything. You can do that later on the home screen."

Space on a screen is tight, and short text looks finished. That is how these lines get written. Shorten only after the full sentence passes the cold-reader check, and check again after shortening.
## Writing UI code

Rules for anyone, human or agent, adding or changing a JusPrin surface. They
exist because every value that is typed by hand drifts from the design system and
from the other side of the app within weeks; today's guards catch most of it, but
only if the code goes through the token file in the first place.

1. **Never type a color, radius, font, or control size.** Every one comes
   from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`. Native code reads it
   through `ShellTheme`: `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for radii,
   spacing, and per-component sizes, `font(role)` for type. A stock
   `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button` is
   dressed through `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, never by calling its setters
   with literals. The Agent page uses only `var(--…)`: `--<group>-<name>` for
   color, `--radius-<name>`, `--font-<role>`, `--font-code`, and
   `--button-<recipe>-padding`.
2. **If the value you need has no token, add the token first.** Put it in
   the JSON, extend the guard in `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` so a
   later edit cannot silently move it, then read it from code. Do not write
   the number "for now": the guards cannot see a literal that is already
   there, and the next reader cannot tell a decision from an accident. A
   value that exists in the design artifacts but not in the roles or scales is a design
   decision to raise, not a reason to type it.
3. **Layout spacing may stay literal, on the scale.** Padding between
   regions, gaps, and margins use 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, or 48 DIP.
   Control padding is not layout spacing; it comes from a button recipe.
4. **Pick the nearest role, never a bespoke size.** The roles are the whole
   type system. Bold at a body or label size is a role of its own; if a
   surface seems to need a size that no role has, see rule 2.
5. **The design system wins when it and the code disagree.** The two Claude
   artifacts are the source of truth (Kenneth, 2026-10-20; Figma is
   retired): the Design System
   (https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL) and the "JusPrin v2"
   canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ). The canvas
   frozen on 2026-10-27 (https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v)
   is history, not a source. Change the token file to match, or, when the
   code's value is the one to keep, change the artifact first. Do not trust
   old commit messages about either.
6. **Run the guards before calling UI work done:** `brand_tokens_tests`,
   `shell_theme_tests`, and `npm test` in `AgentUI`. Then look at the surface
   in the running app; the guards prove the code went through the tokens,
   not that the result looks right.
7. **Upstream files are off limits for style.** OrcaSlicer's own screens are
   retinted through the hooks `BrandPalette.cpp` installs and nothing else;
   see [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md). Their radii and fonts stay
   OrcaSlicer's until the surface is replaced.

## Runtime application in the native app

The token file is applied to the running application in three layers. All
three read `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`; none of them carries a
color literal of its own, and the whole layer touches OrcaSlicer code in only
three small, additive seams plus one attachment point.

1. **Fork-owned surfaces** (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/*`, the React Agent
   page) resolve every style through the token file, not only color.
   - Native: `ShellTheme` exposes `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for
     the radius and spacing scales and the per-component sizes, `font(role)`
     for the type roles above. It is loaded once, by `Brand/BrandPalette.cpp`, and passed
     by reference into every shell widget. Widgets that paint themselves read
     it directly; a stock `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button`
     is dressed through the three functions in `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, so no
     fork-owned C++ file names an OrcaSlicer font preset or writes a radius as
     a number. `tests/jusprin/test_shell_theme.cpp` checks the parse and the
     fonts.
   - Web: `AgentUI/src/tokens.ts` writes the semantic colors as
     `--<group>-<name>` on every appearance change, and once at startup the
     radii as `--radius-<name>` and each type role as a complete `font`
     shorthand, `--font-<role>` in the UI face, plus `--font-code` for the one
     monospace role. The stylesheet may only say `var(--…)` for color, radius,
     and type; `AgentUI/src/styles.test.ts` reads the stylesheet from disk and
     fails on any literal, and on any spacing value off the scale.
   - Canvas: the Prepare canvas's tool strip (`Canvas/ViewportToolStrip`)
     paints with ImGui inside the GL frame, from the same `ShellTheme`. Its
     icons are the `currentColor` SVGs in `resources/jusprin/ui/icons`,
     rasterized white and tinted with the token colour. ImGui 1.83 has no
     shadow primitive, so `elevation.medium` is approximated with stacked
     translucent rounded rectangles.
2. **Retained OrcaSlicer surfaces** are retinted through the color tables
   OrcaSlicer already routes its colors through, installed once per appearance

9:# Error handling
10-
11-An error is **expected** only when a person decided what the product does for that named cause. Every other error is **unexpected**.
12-
13-This repository has no expected-errors table and no reporting function yet.
14-
15-## Expected errors
16-
17-- Each has an entry in the expected-errors table: the cause, what the person sees, and what they can do next. A new entry needs Kenneth's yes; quote his words in the commit message.
18-- A cause is "out of credits" or "no network". A status code, an exception type, or "the request was not valid" is not a cause.
19-- Each entry has a test, and each occurrence is counted.
20-- Handle them with normal control flow, not exceptions.
21-
22-## Unexpected errors
23-
24-- Write no code for them. Do not catch one, give it a default value, retry it, or give it a sentence of its own. Each of those is a guess about a failure nobody understands. It hides the failure and loses where it came from.
25-- Let the failure stop the work and travel up unchanged.
26-- A failure that arrives as a value, such as a status code, stops nothing by itself. Turn it into a thrown error on the spot and stop. Keep the other side's status, request id and error text. Do not interpret it.
27-- One handler at the top of each entry point reports the failure through the one reporting function and tells the person "Something went wrong on our side", with nothing more specific. No other code reports.
28-- When our own code is on both ends, a message that is refused or cannot be read is unexpected.
29-- Never record a failure as a success.
30-- A log line is not a report: it reaches nobody.
31-
32-## Catching
33-
34-- Catch an error only when it is an expected one and the code can recover from it, or at a boundary to translate it or add context, and then rethrow.
35-- Keep lower-level operations strict; the caller that owns the workflow enforces their preconditions.
36-- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering.
37-
38-## Checks
39-
40-- An agent reads the changed code against these rules and asks one question wherever the code decides what happened: did a person decide that outcome?
41-- To audit a commit range or check production for a period, use the `error-handling` skill in the JusPrin repository (`.claude/skills/error-handling/`).

Every error the gateway returns has the body
{"type": "error", "error": {"code": <code>, "message": <message>}} with text
from this table, never bytes from upstream. The client treats 401 as "signed

credits_exhausted adds what the client needs to offer a way on, beside "error";

import json

MESSAGES = {
    'invalid_request': 'The request is not valid.',
    'unknown_model': 'This model is not available.',
    'method_not_allowed': 'This method is not allowed here.',
    'unauthorized': 'Sign in to JusPrin to continue.',
    'quota_exhausted': 'Your JusPrin AI credits for this period are used up.',
    'credits_exhausted': 'You do not have enough credits for this message.',
    'text_too_short': 'A report needs a few sentences.',

    'already_reported': 'This print already has a report.',
    'request_too_large': 'The request is too large.',

    'upstream_error': 'The model service could not answer.',
    'unavailable': 'The model service is unavailable. Try again shortly.',
    'timeout': 'The model service took too long to answer.',
    'busy': 'JusPrin is busy right now. Try again in a moment.',
    'update_required': 'This version of JusPrin can no longer connect to JusPrin accounts. Get the new version to keep using your account.',
}


class GatewayError(Exception):
    """An answer the gateway gives instead of forwarding. Raised inside one
    request and turned into a response at the endpoint boundary only."""

    def __init__(self, status: int, code: str, message: str = None, details: dict = None):
        super().__init__(code)
        self.status = status
        self.code = code
        self.message = message or MESSAGES[code]
        self.details = details

    def body(self) -> bytes:
        return error_body(self.code, self.message, self.details)


def error_body(code: str, message: str = None, details: dict = None) -> bytes:
    return json.dumps({'type': 'error', 'error': {'code': code, 'message': message or MESSAGES[code]},
                       **(details or {})}).encode()


def credits_exhausted(cost: int, balance: int, details: dict) -> GatewayError:
    unit = 'credit' if cost == 1 else 'credits'
    return GatewayError(402, 'credits_exhausted', f'This message needs {cost} {unit}; you have {balance}.', details)

"""POST /ent/jusprin/v2/error_reports: a report of an unexpected error in the
JusPrin desktop app, passed on to the app's Sentry project.

The app sends one only when the person pressed "Report to JusPrin team" or
turned automatic reports on. A report is anonymous: no token is read, and the
body holds only the fields below, the same lines the app's dialog shows under
"See what the report contains".

The Sentry project is the desktop app's own, apart from the server's; its DSN
comes from JUSPRIN_V2_APP_SENTRY_DSN. A server without it cannot pass a report
on, so the request fails like any other fault of the server, and its own Sentry
hears about it.
"""
import json

import sentry_sdk
from django.conf import settings
from django.core.exceptions import ImproperlyConfigured
from django.http import JsonResponse
from django.views.decorators.csrf import csrf_exempt
from django.views.decorators.http import require_POST

from .errors import error_body
from django.http import HttpResponse

# The fields of a report and the longest text each may hold. "where" is the
# stack, from the app's own pages only for now; empty when there is none.
FIELDS = {
    'app': 200,       # "JusPrin 2.0.0 (OrcaSlicer 2.5.0)"
    'os': 200,        # "macOS 26.3"
    'doing': 500,     # what the app was doing, in the app's words
    'error': 8000,    # the error as it reached the top, the other side's text included
    'where': 32000,
}
MAX_BODY_BYTES = 64 * 1024

_client = None


def _sentry_client() -> sentry_sdk.Client:
    global _client
    if _client is None:
        dsn = settings.JUSPRIN_V2_APP_SENTRY_DSN
        if not dsn:
            raise ImproperlyConfigured('JUSPRIN_V2_APP_SENTRY_DSN is not set, so app error reports cannot be passed on')
        # The app's reports are not the server's own errors: a client of
        # their own, with nothing of this request attached.
        _client = sentry_sdk.Client(dsn=dsn, default_integrations=False, send_default_pii=False)
    return _client


def _event(report: dict) -> dict:
    return {
        'level': 'error',
        'platform': 'javascript' if report['where'] else 'native',
        'logger': 'jusprin.app',
        'release': report['app'],
        'message': {'formatted': report['error']},
        'tags': {'doing': report['doing'][:200], 'os': report['os'][:200]},
        'extra': {'doing': report['doing'], 'where': report['where']},
        # One issue per error and what the app was doing, whatever the stack.
        'fingerprint': [report['doing'], report['error']],
    }


@csrf_exempt
@require_POST
def error_reports(request):
    # Our own app is on the other end: a body it could not have sent is
    # refused, and the app treats that as its own unexpected error.
    if len(request.body) > MAX_BODY_BYTES:
        return HttpResponse(error_body('request_too_large'), status=413, content_type='application/json')
    try:
        report = json.loads(request.body)
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError):
        return HttpResponse(error_body('invalid_request'), status=400, content_type='application/json')
    if not isinstance(report, dict) or set(report) != set(FIELDS) or not all(
            isinstance(report[name], str) and len(report[name]) <= limit for name, limit in FIELDS.items()) \
            or not report['error'] or not report['doing']:
        return HttpResponse(error_body('invalid_request'), status=400, content_type='application/json')
    client = _sentry_client()
    event_id = client.capture_event(_event(report))
    return JsonResponse({'id': event_id})

"""POST /ent/jusprin/v2/error_reports: a report of an unexpected error in the
JusPrin desktop app, passed on to the app's Sentry project.

The app sends one only when the person pressed "Report to JusPrin team" or
turned automatic reports on. A report is anonymous: no token is read, and the
body holds only the fields below, the same lines the app's dialog shows under
"See what the report contains".

The Sentry project is the desktop app's own, apart from the server's; its DSN
comes from JUSPRIN_V2_APP_SENTRY_DSN. The report is sent to Sentry before the
app is answered, so the app hears "reported" only once Sentry has it. A server
without the DSN, or a Sentry that refuses the report, fails the request like
any other fault of the server, and the server's own Sentry hears about it.
"""
import json
import uuid
from datetime import datetime, timezone

import requests
from django.conf import settings
from django.core.exceptions import ImproperlyConfigured
from django.http import HttpResponse, JsonResponse
from django.views.decorators.csrf import csrf_exempt
from django.views.decorators.http import require_POST
from sentry_sdk.consts import EndpointType
from sentry_sdk.envelope import Envelope
from sentry_sdk.utils import Dsn

from .errors import error_body

# The fields of a report and the longest text each may hold. "where" is the
# stack, from the app's own pages only for now; empty when there is none.
FIELDS = {
    'app': 200,       # "JusPrin 2.0.0 (OrcaSlicer 2.5.0)"
    'os': 200,        # "macOS 26.3"
    'doing': 500,     # what the app was doing, in the app's words
    'error': 8000,    # the error as it reached the top, the other side's text included
    'where': 32000,
}
MAX_BODY_BYTES = 64 * 1024


def _event(report: dict) -> dict:
    return {
        'event_id': uuid.uuid4().hex,
        'timestamp': datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        'level': 'error',
        'platform': 'javascript' if report['where'] else 'native',
        'logger': 'jusprin.app',
        'release': report['app'],
        'message': {'formatted': report['error']},
        'tags': {'doing': report['doing'][:200], 'os': report['os'][:200]},
        'extra': {'doing': report['doing'], 'where': report['where']},
        # One issue per error and what the app was doing, whatever the stack.
        'fingerprint': [report['doing'], report['error']],
    }


def _send_to_sentry(event: dict) -> None:
    dsn = settings.JUSPRIN_V2_APP_SENTRY_DSN
    if not dsn:
        raise ImproperlyConfigured('JUSPRIN_V2_APP_SENTRY_DSN is not set, so app error reports cannot be passed on')
    auth = Dsn(dsn).to_auth('jusprin-server')
    envelope = Envelope(headers={'event_id': event['event_id']})
    envelope.add_event(event)
    response = requests.post(auth.get_api_url(EndpointType.ENVELOPE), data=envelope.serialize(),
                             headers={'X-Sentry-Auth': auth.to_header(), 'Content-Type': 'application/x-sentry-envelope'},
                             timeout=10)
    response.raise_for_status()


@csrf_exempt
@require_POST
def error_reports(request):
    # Our own app is on the other end: a body it could not have sent is
    # refused, and the app treats that as its own unexpected error.
    if len(request.body) > MAX_BODY_BYTES:
        return HttpResponse(error_body('request_too_large'), status=413, content_type='application/json')
    try:
        report = json.loads(request.body)
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError):
        return HttpResponse(error_body('invalid_request'), status=400, content_type='application/json')
    if not isinstance(report, dict) or set(report) != set(FIELDS) or not all(
            isinstance(report[name], str) and len(report[name]) <= limit for name, limit in FIELDS.items()) \
            or not report['error'] or not report['doing']:
        return HttpResponse(error_body('invalid_request'), status=400, content_type='application/json')
    event = _event(report)
    _send_to_sentry(event)
    return JsonResponse({'id': event['event_id']})

"""POST /ent/jusprin/v2/error_reports: a report from the desktop app reaches
Sentry before the app is answered, and nothing else is passed on."""
import json
import threading
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer

import requests
from django.core.exceptions import ImproperlyConfigured
from django.test import Client, SimpleTestCase, override_settings

URL = '/ent/jusprin/v2/error_reports'
REPORT = {
    'app': 'JusPrin 2.0.0 (OrcaSlicer 2.5.0)',
    'os': 'macOS 26.3',
    'doing': 'exporting G-code from Home',
    'error': "std::filesystem::filesystem_error: filesystem error: in copy_file: Permission denied [\"/tmp/a\"] [\"/tmp/b\"]",
    'where': '',
}


class FakeSentry:
    """A Sentry that keeps what it is sent, and answers with `status`."""

    def __init__(self, status=200):
        self.received = []
        fake = self

        class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
            def do_POST(self):
                fake.received.append((self.path, dict(self.headers), self.rfile.read(int(self.headers['Content-Length']))))
                self.send_response(status)
                self.end_headers()
                self.wfile.write(b'{}')

            def log_message(self, *args):
                pass

        self.server = HTTPServer(('127.0.0.1', 0), Handler)
        threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
        self.dsn = f'http://publickey@127.0.0.1:{self.server.server_port}/16'

    def close(self):
        self.server.shutdown()
        self.server.server_close()

    def event(self):
        path, headers, body = self.received[-1]
        items = body.split(b'\n')
        return path, headers, json.loads(items[2])


class ErrorReportTestCase(SimpleTestCase):
    def post(self, body):
        return Client().post(URL, data=body if isinstance(body, (str, bytes)) else json.dumps(body),
                             content_type='application/json')

    def test_a_report_reaches_the_apps_sentry_project(self):
        sentry = FakeSentry()
        self.addCleanup(sentry.close)
        with override_settings(JUSPRIN_V2_APP_SENTRY_DSN=sentry.dsn):
            response = self.post(REPORT)
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        path, headers, event = sentry.event()
        self.assertEqual(path, '/api/16/envelope/')
        self.assertIn('sentry_key=publickey', headers['X-Sentry-Auth'])
        self.assertEqual(event['event_id'], response.json()['id'])
        self.assertEqual(event['message'], {'formatted': REPORT['error']})
        self.assertEqual(event['release'], REPORT['app'])
        self.assertEqual(event['tags'], {'doing': REPORT['doing'], 'os': REPORT['os']})
        self.assertEqual(event['platform'], 'native')

    def test_a_page_stack_goes_with_the_report(self):
        sentry = FakeSentry()
        self.addCleanup(sentry.close)
        stack = 'TypeError: x is undefined\n    at render (index.js:1:200)'
        with override_settings(JUSPRIN_V2_APP_SENTRY_DSN=sentry.dsn):
            self.assertEqual(self.post({**REPORT, 'where': stack}).status_code, 200)
        event = sentry.event()[2]
        self.assertEqual(event['extra']['where'], stack)
        self.assertEqual(event['platform'], 'javascript')

    def test_a_report_sentry_refuses_is_a_failure_not_an_answer(self):
        sentry = FakeSentry(status=503)
        self.addCleanup(sentry.close)
        with override_settings(JUSPRIN_V2_APP_SENTRY_DSN=sentry.dsn), self.assertRaises(requests.HTTPError):
            self.post(REPORT)

    def test_a_server_without_the_dsn_fails(self):
        with override_settings(JUSPRIN_V2_APP_SENTRY_DSN=''), self.assertRaises(ImproperlyConfigured):
            self.post(REPORT)

    def test_a_body_the_app_could_not_have_sent_is_refused_and_not_passed_on(self):
        sentry = FakeSentry()
        self.addCleanup(sentry.close)
        with override_settings(JUSPRIN_V2_APP_SENTRY_DSN=sentry.dsn):
            for body in ['not json', [REPORT], {**REPORT, 'email': 'a@example.com'}, {k: v for k, v in REPORT.items() if k != 'os'},
                         {**REPORT, 'error': ''}, {**REPORT, 'doing': 7}, {**REPORT, 'error': 'x' * 8001}]:
                with self.subTest(body=str(body)[:60]):
                    self.assertEqual(self.post(body).status_code, 400)
            self.assertEqual(self.post({**REPORT, 'where': 'x' * 70000}).status_code, 413)
        self.assertEqual(sentry.received, [])

    def test_only_post(self):
        self.assertEqual(Client().get(URL).status_code, 405)

# Fork stewardship

**Status:** Required discipline for every change to an upstream-owned file on `jusprin-dev`.

JusPrin is a long-lived fork. Every line it changes in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line it re-resolves at every rebase, forever, by a person who was not there when the line was written. The rules below exist to keep that permanent cost small and, where it cannot be small, to keep it visible.

One question generates all of them: **after this change, what does the fork own?**

- Owning *product policy* is safe. It is ours, upstream will never write it, and it lives in our files.
- Owning a *small neutral seam* is acceptable. It is the kind of thing upstream might plausibly have written itself, so it survives refactors and could be contributed back.
- Owning *upstream's behavior* is the expensive kind. It commits us to re-deriving upstream's intent forever, and the day we take ownership is usually the day the behavior quietly diverges.

Two mechanical facts drive everything else. Git merges text, not meaning: it conflicts when two sides touch the same or adjacent lines, and it stays silent when they touch different lines even if the result is nonsense. And a conflict is a *stop* — a human is forced to look — while silent divergence is unbounded and invisible. Conflicts are therefore not the enemy. Unnoticed drift is, and conflicts that resolve wrongly are.

## The ten principles

### 1. Conflict probability is about where you write, not how much

**Rule.** Place fork edits where upstream rarely writes, and keep the number of distinct sites low.

**Mechanism.** Risk is roughly *how often upstream edits this region* times *how much of the region you occupy*, summed over every place you touched. Each site is an independent draw. New files have probability zero, so their size is free; one line inside a function upstream is actively reworking is expensive.

**The test.** How many separate places does this change touch, and how busy is each one? Would one seam deliver the same capability?

**Violation.** Delivering a single capability through a dozen scattered notification lines across several upstream files, when one funnel that every path already passes through would have carried them.

### 2. A clean merge is not a safe merge

**Rule.** Prefer edits that are locally correct over edits that participate in upstream's control flow.

**Mechanism.** Git merges text. If your edit's correctness depends on the code around it — an ordering, a guard, an early return, an invariant nobody wrote down — upstream can restructure the surroundings, the merge succeeds, and your edit now runs under assumptions that no longer hold, with no signal at all.

**The test.** If upstream restructures the code around this hunk, do I get a conflict or silence? If silence, would any test catch it?

**Violation.** Moving a member out of a constructor's initializer list because a callback can fire mid-construction. Nothing in upstream's code records that invariant, so a future cleanup restores the old form with no conflict and no error.

### 3. Add to upstream's code; do not revise it

**Rule.** Append, insert, and call. Do not rewrite upstream functions or change their signatures.

**Mechanism.** An additive hook fails gracefully: when it conflicts, the resolution is "keep both," and anyone can do that correctly. A rewritten function fails badly: every future upstream change to it is a conflict whose resolution requires re-deriving two intents at once, in code no longer shared with upstream. Rewriting subtle logic also tends to change it, and you find out later.

**The test.** Does upstream's line survive my change? If I deleted or replaced one, why could I not have added next to it?

**Violation.** Replacing OrcaSlicer's undo and redo implementations with fork-owned equivalents in order to learn whether the history position moved. Re-expressing the vendor-specific snapshot walk silently dropped one of its branches. An additive helper that reports the result, leaving upstream's functions untouched, would have answered the same question.

### 4. Own the policy; borrow the mechanism

**Rule.** No product name, color, dimension, or product-specific decision in an upstream-owned file. Upstream files may gain small neutral capabilities; the policy that uses them lives in fork-owned code.

**Mechanism.** Product specifics in upstream files are permanent divergence: they can never be upstreamed and never dropped, so they must be re-resolved forever. A neutral capability — a flag, a getter/setter pair, an event — reads like something upstream could have written, which is exactly why it survives refactors.

**The test.** Would this addition look reasonable in an upstream pull request, with no explanation of our product?

**Violation.** A product-named enum value inside a rendering class, or product decisions embedded in an upstream mouse handler. The fix is a neutral options struct plus a fork-owned controller that applies our policy.

### 5. One seam beats many touch points

**Rule.** Find the single place every path already passes through, and put the fork's line there.

**Mechanism.** Each touch point is an independent conflict draw and an independent thing a future resolver must understand. Collapsing many small recurring costs into one is worth some indirection.

**The test.** Do all the paths I am hooking already converge somewhere downstream? Is there one function that runs exactly when the thing I care about has happened?

**Violation.** Publishing a history-changed event from undo, from redo, and from both history-navigation entry points, when all four funnel through a single update function that runs only on a successful move.

### 6. One shared implementation is worth a guaranteed conflict

**Rule.** When the alternative is two copies of the same behavior, keep the shared path and accept that it will conflict.

**Mechanism.** A conflict is a stop; drift between two copies is silent and unbounded. Trading an invisible risk for a visible, small, recurring one is a good trade.

**The test.** Where did the logic I removed actually go? A move has one implementation; only a duplication risks divergence. If I wrote new behavior beside an existing upstream path rather than calling it, upstream's future improvements will never reach our users.

**Violation.** Writing a second object-duplication routine next to OrcaSlicer's clipboard path and pointing an existing dialog at it. Reusing the existing path — extending it where it was too narrow — keeps one implementation.

### 7. Unavoidable conflicts must be easy to resolve correctly

**Rule.** When you must delete or relocate an upstream line, say at the site what moved, where it went, and what a future rebase must carry across.

# JusPrin's translations

JusPrin shows its interface in the languages OrcaSlicer ships a catalog for
(`languages.json`). OrcaSlicer's own windows translate through upstream's
catalogs in `localization/i18n/`, which the fork never edits. JusPrin's own
text has catalogs of its own here, so taking a new OrcaSlicer release never
conflicts in a translation file:

| Text | Marked with | Catalog | How it reaches the app |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Native windows and text the native side sends to a page | `_L`, `_u8L`, `L`, `_L_CONTEXT`, `_L_PLURAL`, `translated_plural` | `native/<lang>.po`, template `native/JusPrin.pot` | `Brand/brand_catalogs.py` merges it into `resources/i18n/<lang>/<app key>.mo`, the catalog the app loads |
| The AI and Home pages | Lingui macros: `t`, `plural` from `@lingui/core/macro`; `Trans`, `Plural` from `@lingui/react/macro` | `pages/<lang>.po`, one for both pages | `@lingui/vite-plugin` compiles every catalog into each page; the page reads `?lang=` (`AgentUI/src/i18n.tsx`) |

Native text that OrcaSlicer's template already has is left out of
`native/JusPrin.pot`; upstream's translation is used.

## Updating the catalogs

After marking or changing text:

```bash
python3 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py
```

It runs `xgettext` over the native sources and Lingui's extractor over the
pages, then merges the new entries into every language. Translate each new
entry in every `<lang>.po`, following the editing rules in the repository's
`AGENTS.md` (Localization & translations): keep every placeholder and line
break, give each plural form its own inflection, and mark machine
translations `# AI Translated`, adding `# Needs human review: <what>` where
the meaning or the wording is uncertain. `AgentUI/src/catalogs.test.ts` fails
while any entry is untranslated or a translation loses a placeholder.

The page catalogs use ICU placeholders: `{0}`, `{name}`, numbered tags like
`<0>…</0>` for elements inside a `Trans`, and
`{count, plural, one {# printer} other {# printers}}` for counts. Keep the
placeholder and tag names; translate the words, including the words inside a
plural's branches, and give the plural the categories the language uses
(`one`, `few`, `many`, `other`).

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.


Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
The task brief came from the parent session local_cd3120f7-030a-4af8-a6d1-28ecae789f1a. It asks me to turn eleven failures in JusPrin 2 into "unexpected errors" under Kenneth's error-handling rules, and to build the real path they travel:
- one top handler per entry point (native event handlers, page message handlers, and the pages' own top level), which opens the report dialog drawn on boards agent-ui-11 to 16;
- the "report errors automatically" checkbox in Preferences › Updates;
- the sender: app → our server (tsd-enterprise) → Sentry project `jusprin` (id 16).

After that, I remove the per-site handling so each failure travels up unchanged. Each one must be shown in a running scratch copy of the app (its own --datadir and HOME), with what the person sees before and after, and a report reaching the server.

The eleven, by row in /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/designed-refusals-sorted.md, with fuller entries in designed-refusals-outside-ai-requests.md:
- 10: "Signing in didn't finish. Nothing was saved. Try again."
- 11: "JusPrin couldn't start signing in. Try again."
- 16: "The file could not be read." (an attachment)
- 21: "JusPrin couldn't read this file. To try again, choose Printer › Import printers from %s…"
- 39: "The G-code couldn't be written to %s."
- 54: "JusPrin hasn't loaded the AI models for your account yet. Try again in a moment."
- 55: "The panel is still loading. Try again in a moment."
- 58: "Your saved projects couldn't be read…"
- 59: "The open project couldn't be saved, so the file wasn't opened. Try again."
- 60: "Your projects couldn't be loaded. JusPrin will keep trying."
- 71: "The earlier values cannot be put back."

If one of them looks wrong as "Something went wrong on our side" (it is a normal waiting state, or the same sentence also covers a real named cause), I leave it as it is and put it to Kenneth as a question.

The final report says, in plain words for a cold reader: what the person now sees for each of the eleven, what was tested and the result, what is not built, and what is uncommitted where. Its first 400 characters are relayed to the parent, so the outcome goes first.

Rules from the brief, kept verbatim where they bind:
- "No stand-ins. Do not 'log locally for now' or stub the sender. A piece is either built and shown working, or left out and named plainly as not built, with the reason. If one blocker stops a piece (for example the server needs a Sentry DSN you do not have), stop that piece and ask Kenneth the one question, in full, as a question."
- "New on-screen wording beyond what the boards show needs Kenneth's yes: show him the exact strings before calling the work done. Follow the translation rules in AGENTS.md for any string you add or remove."
- Build on a shared Mac: check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja` first, use -j4, one build per build directory, reuse existing dependencies, and do not configure a build the task does not need without asking.
- "Bug-fix rule: reproduce a failure before changing its handling."
- "Do not push, and do not land anything on jusprin-dev or master. Ask Kenneth before committing. Working notes stay untracked and are never added to .gitignore."
- "Never repeat a secret (Sentry token or DSN, API keys) in a message or file."
- "Send no email to made-up addresses and send nothing to the production Sentry project from tests unless Kenneth says so."
- Never drive Kenneth's own running JusPrin.
- Do not copy the main checkout's AGENTS.md into the worktree, and do not commit it. The current rules are uncommitted in /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/AGENTS.md (section "Error handling").
- Do not restore the deleted build-session patch. Add no rule-checking programs (no catch scans, no CI gates).
- Another session is editing Agent/AgentConfiguration.cpp (the save lambdas), AgentHost.cpp (handle_attach_file, store_file_attachment, handle_delete_account), Preferences/PreferencesWindow.cpp and the composer's model picker. Expect to rebase.
- In tsd-enterprise: one local server stack only. Never start a second container, port or database. Edit /Users/kenneth/Projects/tsd-enterprise directly.
- Never commit or stage submodule changes (global CLAUDE.md).
- Global CLAUDE.md lists a Sentry auth token for sentry.obico.io. Never repeat it.
- Never cd into the main checkout. Work in the worktree /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/unexpected-eleven-287b4a (branch claude/unexpected-eleven-287b4a), using absolute paths.

- Shared notes folder: /Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_cd3120f7-030a-4af8-a6d1-28ecae789f1a. It holds error-handling-enforcement.md, from the earlier, deleted build session.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
- The rules, from the main checkout's AGENTS.md:
  - An error is expected only if a person decided the outcome for a named cause.
  - An unexpected error gets no code at the site (no catch, default value, retry or sentence of its own). It travels up unchanged.
  - A failure that arrives as a value is turned into a thrown error on the spot, keeping the other side's status, request id and error text.
  - One top handler per entry point reports it through the one reporting function and says "Something went wrong on our side".
  - A failed tool call is shown in the turn's activity line, not a dialog.
  - When our own code is on both ends, a message that is refused or cannot be read is unexpected.
  - A log line is not a report.
- Kenneth's decisions on the report:
  - Reports are opt-in through the dialog. There is no "report sent" line.
  - Route: app → our server → Sentry, with the DSN read from the server's environment.
  - Stacks are sent, but not shown whole. First version: page stacks only.
  - The provider's error text is kept.
  - One checkbox lives in Preferences › Updates.
  - Tests must not block server releases.
- wxWidgets: an exception that reaches the main loop goes to GUI_App::OnExceptionInMainLoop, whose generic_exception_handle rethrows, and the app ends. A WebKit script-message handler needs its own catch, because an exception must not cross the WebKit callback.
- Fork stewardship: OrcaSlicer-owned files get only small additive seams marked "// JusPrin:". The handback must record the rebase evidence, run with `git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=<last release taken> <newest upstream> HEAD`.
- Translations:
  - Native strings use _L and _L_PLURAL. Page strings use Lingui.
  - Catalogs are updated with `python3 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py`. Every new entry needs translating in all 22 languages, marked "# AI Translated".
  - AgentUI/src/catalogs.test.ts fails while any entry is untranslated.
- Design system: colours, fonts and controls come from ShellTheme via brand_theme(). style_label, style_button and style_primary_button are in Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp. CheckToggle is in Shell/CheckPrintReportPanel.hpp. lucide_bitmap(name, px, colour) is in Shell/LucideIcon.hpp. Layout spacing uses the scale (8, 16, 24…).
- The server address is cloud_server_from_gateway(endpoint_for(config, account_provider())). JUSPRIN_SERVER_URL overrides it, so the scratch app can point at http://localhost:3334.
- tsd-enterprise:
  - The web container runs Django runserver on port 3334, with code mounted so edits reload live.
  - Tests run with `docker compose exec -T web python manage.py test jusprin.v2.tests.<module> --keepdb`.
  - docker-compose.yml is a symlink into the obico-server submodule. Never edit it.

    - `raise_for_status()` makes a refusal from Sentry fail the request instead of answering success.

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.
