Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
- **`@import AppKit` can fail silently in lldb `expr`** ("no known method '-windows'"). Then cast everything to `id` and get classes with `((Class(*)(const char*))objc_getClass)("NSApplication")`; a working runner that runs a JS file in the chat panel (title "JusPrin Agent") was `runjs.sh` in the 2026-11-12 scratchpad.
- **The composer's model picker is a drop-down the background `app_click` refuses.** Click it from page JS via the runner above. OpenRouter's list labels models "Anthropic: Claude …", so a regex on "Claude Fable" picks OpenRouter's copy; the Anthropic-key one starts with "Claude".
- **A slice right after lldb attaches hung once (2026-11-12).** The worker sat in upstream `name_tbb_thread_pool_threads_set_locale()`, a barrier every TBB thread must reach, and the main thread waited in `BackgroundSlicingProcess::start()` forever. After a relaunch with no debugger the same slice ran at once. Suspected trigger: pausing the app while its thread pool was starting. Don't report such a hang as an app bug without a run that had no debugger attached.
- **A locked screen slows the whole app 2-4×** (2026-11-05: the same first-launch OrcaSlicer import took 46 s unlocked at 15:48, 226 s locked at 19:22, same build and folder). Compare timings only between back-to-back runs under the same conditions, old and new builds side by side.

For fork-owned wx controls, split painting from the paint event —
`paint(wxPaintEvent&)` builds the DC and delegates to
`draw(wxDC&, wxGraphicsContext&, wxSize)` — then add `snapshot()` that draws into
a `wxMemoryDC` over a `wxBitmap`. The shell harness writes those PNGs each run
(honour an env var like `JUSPRIN_ARTIFACT_DIR`; the harness deletes its temp data
dir at exit, so artifacts written there vanish before you can look).

Note `wxGraphicsContext::Create` has no generic `wxDC` overload — each caller
must build the context for its own concrete DC and pass it in.

**Why:** on the printer/spool chip slice, 267 green harness checks coexisted with
two real rendering defects, both found only by opening the image: a long-name
snapshot byte-identical to the normal one (the capture helper called `refresh()`
first, which re-read the store and undid the test's label — so the width
assertion compared a value to itself), and an inline detail overrunning the
trailing chevron under width pressure (measured width was correct; the overlap
was a painting error). Screen-control access was denied and `screencapture`
could not see the window, so in-app rendering was the only route.

"light differs from dark", "long name differs from normal" — so a silently
reverted label fails instead of passing. Then still *open the image*; the
assertions prove difference, not correctness. See

Resolve the conflicts, then `git commit`. A later patch release on the same release branch, such as 2.5.1 after 2.5.0, needs no override: a plain `git merge` finds the right base.

**The test.** Is the merge base the release we last took, and not a commit on upstream's development line?

**Violation.** `git merge upstream/main` or `git merge v2.5.0` with no base given. Each produces thousands of conflicts in files JusPrin never edited.

## Before you finish

A change that touches upstream-owned files is not done until this is recorded in the handback or pull request:

1. **The rebase simulation and its result.** Run it against the newest upstream release, with the release the fork last took as the base (rule 10), and name both endpoint commits — measurements are not reproducible otherwise.

   ```bash
   git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=<last release taken> <newest upstream release> HEAD
   ```

   For each conflicted file, state whether the natural resolution is correct or lossy. A lossy one is a defect to fix now, not a note for later.

2. **An account of every upstream line deleted or rewritten.** Where the logic went, and why an additive form was not possible.

3. **A statement of what the fork now owns.** Policy, a neutral seam, or upstream behavior. The third needs an explicit justification.

An automatic merge is evidence about today's text. It is not proof that a future rebase will merge, and never proof that the merged result behaves correctly. After every upstream update, run the focused contract tests, the full native build, the real multi-plate workflow, native gizmo input, and the stock-behavior regression checks.

## This fork's terrain

Facts specific to OrcaSlicer, worth knowing before choosing where to put a seam. They change over time; re-measure rather than trusting these.

`Plater.cpp` is by far the busiest file the fork touches, followed by the central `src/slic3r/CMakeLists.txt`, `GLCanvas3D.cpp`, and `PartPlate.cpp`. `GLToolbar` and `GLGizmosManager` are quiet. File-level churn is only a first approximation: some functions inside `Plater.cpp` have not been touched upstream in the entire life of this fork, and a seam there is far cheaper than the file's overall rate suggests. Measure the function, not just the file.

Some native state is shared rather than owned by one object. OrcaSlicer's collapse toolbar belongs to `Plater` and is used by both the Prepare and Preview canvases, so a per-canvas guard cannot save and restore it correctly. Shared state needs one owner at the shared lifetime boundary, and exact restoration needs a getter as well as a setter.

"""lldb: drive the open ErrorReportDialog through its own functions.
act(pid, steps): steps from 'open' (toggle_contents), 'tick' (the box's
CheckToggle::toggle, as a click does), 'report' (EndModal(wxID_OK)),
'cancel' (EndModal(wxID_CANCEL))."""
import lldb, struct
import winshot

def _addr(target, name):
    found = target.FindFunctions(name)
    for i in range(found.GetSize()):
        sym = found.GetContextAtIndex(i).GetSymbol()
        if sym.IsValid() and sym.GetName() == name:
            return sym.GetStartAddress().GetLoadAddress(target)
    raise RuntimeError('no symbol ' + name)

def _call(frame, expr):
    opts = lldb.SBExpressionOptions(); opts.SetLanguage(lldb.eLanguageTypeC_plus_plus)
    opts.SetTryAllThreads(False); opts.SetTimeoutInMicroSeconds(20_000_000)
    v = frame.EvaluateExpression(expr, opts)
    if v.GetError().Fail() and 'no result' not in (v.GetError().GetCString() or ''):
        raise RuntimeError(v.GetError().GetCString())
    return v

def act(pid, steps):
    target, process, frame = winshot._attach(pid)
    try:
        current = _addr(target, 'Slic3r::GUI::JusPrin::ErrorReportDialog::current()')
        theme_fn = _addr(target, 'Slic3r::GUI::JusPrin::brand_theme()')
        dlg = _call(frame, '((void*(*)())%d)()' % current).GetValueAsUnsigned()
        theme = _call(frame, '((void*(*)())%d)()' % theme_fn).GetValueAsUnsigned()
        if not dlg:
            raise RuntimeError('no report dialog is open')
        err = lldb.SBError()
        raw = process.ReadMemory(dlg, 8192, err)
        words = struct.unpack('<1024Q', raw)
        at = words.index(theme)  # m_theme, then m_chevron, m_contents, m_automatic, m_cancel, m_report
        automatic = words[at + 3]
        print('dialog 0x%x box 0x%x' % (dlg, automatic))
        for step in steps:
            if step == 'open':
                _call(frame, '((void(*)(void*))%d)((void*)%d)' % (_addr(target, 'Slic3r::GUI::JusPrin::ErrorReportDialog::toggle_contents()'), dlg))
            elif step == 'tick':
                _call(frame, '((void(*)(void*))%d)((void*)%d)' % (_addr(target, 'Slic3r::GUI::JusPrin::CheckToggle::toggle()'), automatic))
            elif step in ('report', 'cancel'):
                _call(frame, '((void(*)(void*, int))%d)((void*)%d, %d)' % (_addr(target, 'wxDialog::EndModal(int)'), dlg, 5100 if step == 'report' else 5101))
            print('STEP', step)
    finally:
        process.Detach()
EOF

"""Serves the instrumented page; /log?x is printed, /next hands out the next
scenario name written to the file `next` (once)."""
import os, sys, urllib.parse
from http.server import SimpleHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer
ROOT = sys.argv[2]
class H(SimpleHTTPRequestHandler):
    def __init__(self, *a, **k): super().__init__(*a, directory=ROOT, **k)
    def do_GET(self):
        if self.path.startswith('/log?'):
            print('LOG', urllib.parse.unquote(self.path[5:]), flush=True); self.send_response(204); self.end_headers(); return
        if self.path == '/next':
            p = os.path.join(ROOT, 'next'); name = ''
            if os.path.exists(p): name = open(p).read(); os.remove(p)
            self.send_response(200); self.send_header('Content-Type', 'text/plain'); self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(name.encode()); return
        return super().do_GET()
    def do_POST(self):
        if self.path == '/snap':
            body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers['Content-Length']))
            n = len([f for f in os.listdir(ROOT) if f.startswith('snap-')])
            open(os.path.join(ROOT, 'snap-%02d.html' % n), 'wb').write(body)
            print('SNAP snap-%02d.html' % n, flush=True)
        self.send_response(204); self.end_headers()
    def log_message(self, *a): pass
HTTPServer(('127.0.0.1', int(sys.argv[1])), H).serve_forever()

content.text:
Everything you asked to see live is now shown, except row 71, which can't happen in the real app. While testing I found the reports were leaking file paths, which can include project names, and fixed that. Nothing is committed or pushed. The scratch app sent its reports through the local server to a stand-in Sentry on this Mac, not the real Sentry project.

- **Row 39, a G-code export that can't be written:** I put a saved G-code copy in a scratch project and had Home export it into a read-only folder. The dialog opened, and the report reached the stand-in Sentry.
  - **Leak fixed:** the report's error text held both full file paths. An export's file name usually contains the project name, which breaks the dialog's promise of "no files, no project names".
  - **Now:** a file-system error's paths are replaced with `<path>` (in `Support/ErrorReport.cpp`). I rebuilt, ran it again, and the dialog and the sent report both show `["<path>"] ["<path>"]`.
- **Row 55, the printer chat with no instructions:** I made the printer chat page hold back its instructions, then sent a message. The dialog opened and Report delivered the report.
  - **After the dialog:** the person sees their own message with nothing under it: no reply and no "thinking" line. The reply box stays ready.
  - **Sending again:** each new message opens the dialog again.
- **Row 71, an undo refused without a reason:** it can't be triggered without changing product code. The app's settings check records a reason every time it refuses, so a refusal with no reason never happens. Only the unit test, using a fake workspace, shows it.
- **The Preferences box:** Preferences › Updates showed "Report errors to the JusPrin team automatically" unticked. Ticking it saved `true` to the settings file.
- **Automatic sending:** with the box on, the next error went straight to the stand-in Sentry and no error dialog opened.

**Still open:** other kinds of error can still name a file. For example, an OrcaSlicer error message that includes a file name only has the home folder replaced with "~". There's no general way to strip file names from any error text. So either the dialog's "no files, no project names" promise gets softened, or we accept the risk; that's Kenneth's call.

I've stopped the app and the test servers, put back tsd-enterprise's `.env` and restarted its web container, and deleted the scratch data folders. **Mechanism.** The fork follows upstream's release branches, and each release branch splits off upstream's development line on its own. A plain merge picks the common ancestor itself, a development-line commit from before both release branches. Its conflict list is then everything that differs between the two release branches: vendor profiles, translations, CI files, none of it ours. Naming the last release we took as the base limits the merge to the fork's own changes. That gives the same conflicts a replay would hit, resolved once, with no commits rewritten, so branches in progress merge forward without a rebase. Measured on 2026-11-07, going from v2.4.2 to v2.5.0: 22 conflicted files either way, and a branch in progress merged into the trial result with no conflicts.

**How.** In a worktree on a new branch from `jusprin-dev`, the development branch:

```bash
git rev-parse <new release>^{commit} > "$(git rev-parse --git-dir)/MERGE_HEAD"
git merge-recursive <last release taken> -- HEAD <new release>
```

Resolve the conflicts, then `git commit`. A later patch release on the same release branch, such as 2.5.1 after 2.5.0, needs no override: a plain `git merge` finds the right base.

**The test.** Is the merge base the release we last took, and not a commit on upstream's development line?

**Violation.** `git merge upstream/main` or `git merge v2.5.0` with no base given. Each produces thousands of conflicts in files JusPrin never edited.

## Before you finish

A change that touches upstream-owned files is not done until this is recorded in the handback or pull request:

1. **The rebase simulation and its result.** Run it against the newest upstream release, with the release the fork last took as the base (rule 10), and name both endpoint commits — measurements are not reproducible otherwise.

   ```bash
   git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=<last release taken> <newest upstream release> HEAD
   ```

   For each conflicted file, state whether the natural resolution is correct or lossy. A lossy one is a defect to fix now, not a note for later.

2. **An account of every upstream line deleted or rewritten.** Where the logic went, and why an additive form was not possible.

3. **A statement of what the fork now owns.** Policy, a neutral seam, or upstream behavior. The third needs an explicit justification.

An automatic merge is evidence about today's text. It is not proof that a future rebase will merge, and never proof that the merged result behaves correctly. After every upstream update, run the focused contract tests, the full native build, the real multi-plate workflow, native gizmo input, and the stock-behavior regression checks.

Report unexpected errors to the JusPrin team, and stop explaining five that can't happen

When something fails that no person can act on, JusPrin now shows one
dialog, "Something went wrong on our side" (boards agent-ui-11 to 16),
instead of a sentence about that particular failure. The person can see
the whole report, press "Report to JusPrin team", or tick "From now on,
report errors like this automatically". The report goes to JusPrin's
server (/ent/jusprin/v2/error_reports), which passes it to Sentry.

Why: under the error-handling rules in AGENTS.md, a failure with no
outcome a person decided travels up unchanged to the top of its entry
point, and is reported there, instead of each site writing its own
sentence. Kenneth agreed to this on 2026-11-15: "Yes, go with this
approach."

The reporting path
- Support/ErrorReport: report_unexpected_error() logs the error, then
  sends it at once when automatic reports are on, or queues it for the
  dialog after the current event. A failure that repeats while its
  dialog waits is queued once. A report holds the app and OS versions,
  what the app was doing, the error and, for page errors, the stack. The
  home folder becomes "~", a file-system error's paths become "<path>",
  and each field is cut to the server's limit. The send is anonymous: no
  token or cookie.
- Shell/ErrorReportDialog: the dialog, drawn with the design tokens.
- Top handlers: OrcaSlicer's main-loop exception hook (one line in
  GUI_App::OnExceptionInMainLoop; running out of memory still goes to
  OrcaSlicer's own handling), the AI pages' and Home's message handlers,
  and both pages' own top level (window "error" and
  "unhandledrejection", sent as a new report_error message and queued
  until the page has connected).
- Preferences › Updates: a new "Error reports" box,
  "Report errors to the JusPrin team automatically", off by default.

Five failures now take that path, with their sentences removed:
- "JusPrin couldn't start signing in. Try again." (the AI page and Home)
- "The file could not be read." (an attachment that is not base64, or a
  picked file that cannot be opened or read)
- "The G-code couldn't be written to %s." (exporting from print history)
- "The panel is still loading. Try again in a moment." (a printer or
  filament chat asked to reply before its page sent its instructions)
- "The earlier values cannot be put back." (an undo the settings preview
  refuses without giving a reason)

Six others stay as they are, on Kenneth's answer "Yes, keep them":
signing in that did not finish, an unreadable import from another app,
the AI models not loaded yet, the saved projects that could not be
read, the open project that could not be saved, and projects that could
not be loaded.

New on-screen strings beyond the boards (the report's row names "App",
"Was doing" and "Where", the singular forms of the two counted
sentences, and the Preferences group, box and detail line) were shown to
Kenneth, who answered "approved". All new strings are machine-translated
into the 22 catalogs and marked "# AI Translated"; two are also marked
"Needs human review" (the Lithuanian and Basque singular forms).

Tests
- agent_bridge_tests (580 cases), jusprin_tests (178),
  jusprin_profile_tests (20) and shell_theme_tests (17) pass;
  brand_tokens_tests has its one known failure. AgentUI vitest (830,
  catalog completeness included) and the HomeUI tests pass; tsc is clean
  for both. These ran before the last change, which only touches
  Support/ErrorReport.cpp (not in any test target); the app was rebuilt
  and checked live after it.
- Shown in a scratch copy of the app (its own data folder and HOME), with
  reports going through the local server to a stand-in Sentry:
  - sign-in that cannot start: the dialog opens; Cancel sends nothing.
  - an attachment that is not base64: the dialog opens; with the box
    ticked the button reads "Report this and future errors", the report
    arrives, and the setting is saved as on.
  - G-code export beside a file in a read-only folder: the dialog opens
    and the report arrives, with both paths shown as "<path>".
  - a printer chat whose page held back its instructions: the dialog
    opens and the report arrives. The person then sees their message
    with no reply under it and the reply box ready; each further
    message opens the dialog again.
  - an error thrown in the AI page's own script: the dialog opens and
    the report arrives.
  - the Preferences box: shown off, ticked, saved as on; the next error
    is sent with no dialog.
- Unit tests only: a picked attachment that cannot be read from disk
  (needs a real drop or the file picker), and the undo refused without
  a reason. The undo case cannot happen in the real app:
  OrcaWorkspaceAdapter::preview_settings records a reason with every
  refusal, so only the fake workspace can produce it.

OrcaSlicer-owned file
- GUI_App.cpp gains two lines at the top of OnExceptionInMainLoop and
  nothing upstream is deleted or rewritten; the hook is reached through
  JusPrin/OrcaHooks.hpp, which GUI_App.cpp already includes. The fork
  now owns policy here: an exception that leaves an event handler is
  reported and the app keeps running, where OrcaSlicer's own handler
  showed its error and went on.
- Rebase check: git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=v2.5.0
  (40ecc66f78) v2.5.1 (eef7710cb1) against this change merges
  GUI_App.cpp cleanly, since upstream did not change it. The only
  conflict, src/OrcaSlicer.cpp, is the same without this change.
